subject: Per-token tier reconciliation and AWS/GCP marketplace billing impact
messages:
From: Sarah Patel <procurement@acme.com>

Cc: legal@acme.com

Subject: Clarify: per-token volume discounts + marketplace billing impact

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. Two quick asks from procurement before we move to legal:

2) We plan to route payments through AWS Marketplace initially. How does that change the net price to us? Specifically: does Redwood apply the same committed-tier discounts when a customer purchases via marketplace, or do marketplace fees reduce the effective discount?

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Patel <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-token volume discounts + marketplace billing impact

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear asks. High level first, then I'll attach a simple spreadsheet with numbers.

Short answers:
- Per-token commitments: we publish a baseline per-token price and then layer committed discounts by monthly/annual committed spend. Typical example (examples only - final commercial will be in the SOW):
  • 0–250M tokens: $0.000020 / token (no commit)
  • 250M–1B tokens: $0.000016 / token (10% off baseline)
  • 1B+ tokens: $0.000012 / token (40% off baseline)
- Marketplace impact: marketplace platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure) charge a platform fee (typically 10–15%). If a customer purchases via the marketplace listing, the marketplace takes its fee out of the gross invoice, which reduces the net revenue we receive. By default, our public marketplace listing shows the gross price; the net price we can honor after marketplace fees would need to be adjusted unless we agree to absorb some or all of the fee.

Options we typically use depending on deal size:
1) Direct billing under a committed plan (preferred for discounts): customer signs a Redwood SOW and invoices are sent directly to the customer. Marketplace listing remains for procurement tracking only. This preserves full committed discounts because no marketplace fee is deducted from Redwood.
2) Marketplace purchase with pass-through adjustment: customer pays via marketplace; Redwood lists a gross price on the marketplace. We then apply a monthly credit equivalent to the marketplace fee so the customer effectively receives the committed-tier net price. This requires a reconciliation process (we provide a monthly credit note).
3) Absorb fee: Redwood reduces its list discount to cover marketplace fees (rare for small deals; used as a competitive concession for strategic accounts).

Trade-offs:
- Option 1 gives clean economics for us and the customer; procurement can still track spend through the marketplace if they need, but finance will accept a direct invoice.
- Option 2 is easiest for procurement but adds operational reconciliation work on our side and can complicate revenue recognition unless we mark credits in the invoice flow.
- Option 3 is simple for procurement and ops but reduces Redwood revenue — we typically reserve this for large, strategic commitments.

I attached a quick pricing model (redwood-pricing-model-2026.xlsx) that shows example gross vs net numbers under a 12% marketplace fee and three commitment tiers.

Next steps I propose:
- Rafael to confirm preferred option with Redwood finance (cc: Ben) — by EOD 12/2
- If Acme prefers marketplace purchase, we'll draft the credit/reconciliation clause in the SOW and specify monthly credit notes
- If Acme prefers direct billing, we update the SOW to reflect Redwood invoicing cadence and sign via DocuSign

Happy to join a short call with procurement + finance to finalize.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Dec 2026 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Clarify: per-token volume discounts + marketplace billing impact

Ben — looping you in to validate the options Rafael outlined. Key asks from Acme: keep committed-tier economics intact; they'd prefer to start via AWS Marketplace for procurement reasons but are open to direct billing if it speeds contracting.

Questions for finance/ops (can you confirm by EOD 12/2):
- Can finance handle monthly credit notes that reflect a marketplace fee (we'd issue a credit that brings the marketplace purchase to the committed net price)?
- Would issuing credits like this materially change revenue recognition or create additional compliance overhead?
- If we propose a hybrid (90-day pilot direct-bill, then marketplace procurement afterwards), are there legal/ops flags we should include in the SOW?

Suggested language for SOW if they want marketplace purchase + credits:
"Redwood will list services for purchase on the Marketplace. For Marketplace purchases, Redwood will issue monthly credit notes equivalent to the platform fee charged by the Marketplace, to align the customer's net paid price to the committed-tier pricing set forth in this Agreement. The parties agree to reconcile Marketplace invoices monthly."

If credits are a no-go from finance, we can instead offer an increased commit floor to cover the marketplace fee and preserve net economics. Example: if Acme wants a 20% discount and the marketplace fee is 12%, we could require a higher committed spend to net-sustain the program.

Rafael — flagging for your commercial input on commit thresholds.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Enterprise
redwood.ai

From: Sarah Patel <procurement@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify: per-token volume discounts + marketplace billing impact

Marissa / Rafael — thanks for the detailed notes. I reviewed with Acme finance; they prefer to start the procurement via AWS Marketplace to align with internal purchasing controls, but they are comfortable with a hybrid approach you suggested. Proposed path:

1) 90-day pilot: Redwood invoices Acme directly (committed pilot pricing in SOW).
2) Post-pilot: purchase transitions to AWS Marketplace. Redwood issues monthly credit notes equal to the marketplace platform fee so our net spend equals the committed-tier pricing.

Action items:
- Rafael to send an updated SOW reflecting the 90-day pilot / direct-bill clause + marketplace transition language (we need this for our procurement legal).
- Please include the proposed credit language verbatim and a sample invoice/credit note illustration (helpful for our AP team).
- I can route the SOW for signature once we have DocuSign ready.

Would appreciate DocuSign link and the updated SOW by EOD Friday 12/4.

Thanks,
Sarah Patel
